interface.name: nextspace_application_v1
interface.description: This interface controls only a client's own xdg toplevels. It grants no authority over other clients, the desktop shell, activation or output settings. Standard xdg-shell remains sufficient when this extension is unavailable; absolute positioning then degrades to compositor-chosen placement.

entry.name: invalid_surface
entry.summary: surface is not an owned xdg toplevel

entry.name: duplicate_window
entry.summary: surface already has a window object

event.name: work_areas_reset

description.summary: begin a complete read-only work-area snapshot

event.description: Sent on binding and whenever output geometry or shell reservations change. Applications cannot set reservations. Coordinates are logical desktop units with a top-left origin; names match xdg-output.name. Replace the preceding snapshot only at work_areas_done. This does not change ordinary window placement or grant authority over other clients.

interface.name: nextspace_window_v1
interface.description: Positions use the top-left of the complete logical window frame in desktop units. With client-side decorations this is xdg window geometry; with negotiated server decorations it includes the compositor's frame insets. Requests are suggestions. The compositor keeps a usable part of the window on an available output and sends the authoritative position after mapping, moving or resizing. Clients must not assume synchronous placement. A window object must be destroyed before its xdg toplevel or wl_surface.

event.name: preferred_output
event.description: The name matches xdg-output.name. An empty name means no preferred output is currently visible. Fractional-scale still owns backing density.

request.name: set_accepts_focus

description.summary: decline keyboard focus for auxiliary windows

request.description: A zero value prevents this window from taking keyboard focus. This is suitable for application menus and icons that receive pointer events while their document keeps keyboard focus. The default is one. A nonzero value permits ordinary compositor focus policy; it does not activate a window or grant authority to choose the focused application.

request.name: set_level
request.description: Set the AppKit logical window level. Values are constrained to -1000 through 1000. Focus and ordering stay within that level. This metadata grants neither shell authority nor a secure screen-lock role.

request.name: order

description.summary: order among owned peers in the same level

request.description: A positive value orders above the reference, a negative value below. A null reference orders at the top or bottom of the level. References in another level and zero direction are ignored. Ordering does not change keyboard focus or activate an application.

request.name: set_minimized

description.summary: restore or minimize this owned window

request.description: This changes visibility without destroying the surface or its retained contents. The compositor sends the resulting state asynchronously.

request.name: set_metadata

description.summary: owned AppKit identity and client frame geometry

request.description: client_id is meaningful only inside this client's process. style is the AppKit style mask. title_height is the client-drawn title strip in logical surface units, or zero for a borderless window. These are presentation hints and grant no authority over other clients or session security.

request.name: prepare_drag

description.summary: action masks for the next owned pointer drag

request.description: Set the local and external data-device action masks for the next serial-authorized drag originating from this window or its popups. Local means the destination shares this Wayland connection. The masks may contain only copy and move; they are intersected with the source's advertised actions. The compositor chooses the appropriate mask before offering data to each destination. This changes neither input authority nor another client's source. A new request replaces the pending values.

event.name: drag_context

description.summary: validated pointer-drag context for an owned surface

event.description: Sent only for a serial-authorized pointer drag. begin, motion, drop and cancel describe the producer's gesture. enter describes the destination after wl_data_device.enter. surface belongs to the receiving client and may be a popup of this window. id identifies the gesture, including while a completed drop waits for a receiver's decision. local is one only when producer and destination use the same Wayland connection. x and y are logical desktop pointer coordinates with a top-left origin. These events grant no authority and do not replace data-device action negotiation or completion. Applications must use wl_data_source.dnd_finished to decide whether their data was successfully transferred.

request.name: set_presented

description.summary: order an owned window in or out without losing its state

request.description: A zero value hides the surface and its popups without destroying the toplevel. A nonzero value restores presentation. Shade, desktop, stacking level, geometry and minimization remain unchanged. This does not grant activation or authority over another client's windows.

request.name: set_frame_extents

description.summary: retain native logical frame metrics with server decorations

request.description: These logical insets preserve the application's frame/content geometry when xdg-decoration selects a server frame. They do not decorate a client-side window or grant placement, focus or shell authority. Each inset must be in 0..128; an invalid request is ignored in its entirety. The latest valid request applies at the next wl_surface.commit. The default frame remains in effect when this request is not used. A zero top inset omits the title, and zero side/bottom insets omit those edges. Controls follow the owned AppKit style metadata. Fullscreen omits the frame while retaining these metrics for restoration.

request.name: set_document_edited
request.description: A nonzero value selects the edited close-button artwork; zero restores the clean artwork. The default is zero. This presentation hint applies immediately and survives hiding or minimization. It changes no close, activation, placement or shell policy.

request.name: set_title_state
request.description: The default is normal. This hint applies immediately without a surface commit; invalid values are ignored. Actual keyboard focus always selects the key appearance. The main appearance is allowed only while another window on this same Wayland connection has keyboard focus. A key hint on an unfocused window does not select key appearance or change focus. This grants no activation, placement or shell authority.

request.name: begin_color_pick
request.description: Begin a compositor-controlled magnifier interaction after a left-button release or Space/Enter key press delivered to this window. The serial must identify that recent, unconsumed gesture. Forged, expired, replayed, hidden-window and busy requests finish with unavailable. Only one pick may run at a time. The compositor provides a visible magnifier, previews pointer changes, selects on the next left-button release, and cancels on Escape or a right-button click. Other applications receive no selection click. This grants no general screen-capture access. Colors are opaque displayed sRGB channel values, excluding the cursor. Each request receives exactly one terminal event while its window object remains alive.

request.name: cancel_color_pick

description.summary: Cancel this window's matching active pick

request.description: An inactive or mismatched request is ignored. Destroying or unmapping the owner, locking the session, or changing the output layout also ends an active pick. A client must use a fresh request ID for every attempt.
